comparison: Both strongly support the CE-MS data (C4, C51, C64-C66, C70, C83, C176) as high-quality and central to the study. OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive methodological rigor including recovery rates and cell volume measurements (C52-C55), while peer reviewers focus on the technical quality and kinetic insights. Both agree these experiments demonstrate quantitative measurements of inositol pyrophosphates under different phosphate conditions.

Both support the mutant analysis data (C56-C59, C61-C63). OpenEval groups these with broader CE-MS findings, while peer reviewers specifically highlight the loss-of-function phenotypes in kcs1 and vip1 mutants. Both describe the experiments as high technical quality that advance understanding of inositol pyrophosphate metabolism kinetics.

Both support the quantitative approach to physiological concentrations (C52-C55). OpenEval emphasizes these measurements as providing methodological rigor, while peer reviewers specifically praise the consideration of physiological levels as critical to interpretation and a key strength of the manuscript.

Both strongly support the genetic correlation analysis (C72-C74, C76-C82, C86-C88, C91-C92) linking 1,5-IP8 depletion to PHO pathway activation. OpenEval emphasizes the systematic epistasis analysis across multiple mutants, while peer reviewers highlight the well-argued correlation between PP-InsP levels, dynamics, and mutant phenotypes. Both agree this provides compelling evidence for 1,5-IP8 as the critical regulator.

Both support the conclusion that 1,5-IP8 is the phosphate nutrient messenger (C89-C90, C104-C105, C147). OpenEval emphasizes the systematic mutant analysis and threshold data in vip1Δ cells, while peer reviewers accept this as the central conclusion with the editor stating it provides 'compelling data.' Both evaluations find the evidence convincing.

Both support the vip1Δ time-course analysis and threshold interpretation (C93-C99, C172-C173). OpenEval emphasizes this as compelling evidence for 1,5-IP8 specificity, while peer reviewers accept the logic connecting 5-IP7 overaccumulation to delayed activation. Both find the correlation analysis well-argued.

Both support the Pho81ΔSPX phenotype data (C110-C112) demonstrating the SPX domain requirement for PHO pathway induction. OpenEval groups this with broader SPX domain analysis, while peer reviewers specifically note this demonstrates genetic-level evidence for SPX domain function. No challenges to these findings from either evaluation.

Both support the K154A mutation data (C116-C118, C121) as evidence that disrupting inositol pyrophosphate binding mimics Pi starvation. OpenEval emphasizes the consistency with structural analysis, while peer reviewers acknowledge the phenotypic observations as part of accepted genetic analysis, though noting limitations in molecular mechanism detail.

Both support the reinterpretation of random mutagenesis data (C122-C125). OpenEval emphasizes consistency with structural analysis strengthening the conclusion, while peer reviewers accept this as part of the structure-function analysis using reverse genetics. Both find the structural reasoning consistent with the overall model.

Divergent evaluations of molecular mechanism (C6, C121). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting Western blot confirmation and consistency across experiments, though acknowledging reliance on genetic inference over direct biochemical demonstration. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting limited insight into molecular mechanism due to lack of complementary in vitro binding assays or co-IP experiments, attributed to technical limitations.

Both support the genetic rescue experiments (C131-C133, C135-C138) demonstrating that disrupting inositol pyrophosphate signaling compensates for minimum domain defects. OpenEval notes the experiments provide direct evidence but rely on genetic inference, while peer reviewers accept the observations as part of structure-function analysis, noting desire for additional biochemical validation but not challenging the genetic findings.

Both support the SPX domain-only construct experiments (C140-C145) as evidence for SPX-Pho85-Pho80 interaction. OpenEval emphasizes these provide direct evidence for the interaction, while peer reviewers accept the localization observations as part of the reverse genetics approach, expressing desire for complementary biochemical assays but not challenging the validity of the findings.

Both support the AlphaFold structural predictions (C126-C129) and their validation by consistency with mutant phenotypes. OpenEval notes the model relies heavily on computational prediction, while peer reviewers accept the structural interpretation as part of the model, with one reviewer praising it as providing 'a vivid model for regulation.' Neither challenges the structural predictions.

Both strongly support the integrated model (C146, C148, C187-C192) as internally consistent with all experimental evidence. OpenEval notes the model successfully explains contradictory observations but has limited direct biochemical evidence for proposed mechanisms. Peer reviewers unanimously accept the model, with the editor stating it 'suggests a unifying mechanism across eukaryotes.' Both find the unified framework compelling.

Both support the reinterpretation of prior work (C3, C30, C44-C45, C174). OpenEval emphasizes that CE-MS data directly contradicts earlier radio-HPLC findings and the critique is logically sound. Peer reviewers explicitly state the authors 'demonstrate convincingly' that previous studies were misleading and that resolving this confusion is of significant importance to the community. Strong agreement on this correction.

Both support the identification of discrepancies with prior in vitro work (C177-C182). OpenEval emphasizes the Kd mismatch and in vitro vs in vivo discrepancies as logically sound critiques. Peer reviewers accept these observations as part of the convincing demonstration that previous studies were misleading. Both evaluations agree the discrepancies are resolved by the current study.

Divergent evaluations of cross-species generalization (C8, C193). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting that extension to plants and mammals relies heavily on literature interpretation and requires additional experimental validation, particularly for plant data showing complexity. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, with explicit statements that authors 'provided strong support' for IP8 regulation across eukaryotes including animals and plants.

Both support the yeast-specific findings (C168-C169) from this study. OpenEval groups these with broader cross-species synthesis and finds the yeast data supportive while questioning extension to other organisms. Peer reviewers praise the yeast CE-MS experiments as central and of high technical quality. Agreement on yeast data quality, but OpenEval more cautious about broader implications.

OpenEval supports background and contextual claims (C1-C2, C10-C21, C32-C43) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers focused on experimental findings rather than background material.

OpenEval supports miscellaneous claims (C7, C9, C60, C119, C187) as either established knowledge or reasonable inferences from data. No direct corresponding peer review evaluation found, though some claims overlap with other peer evaluations (e.g., C187 appears in R10).
